article_content: Family and friends remember slain American journalist James Foley as a compassionate and deeply principled reporter who sought to highlight the humanity of those caught in conflict. At age 40, Foley was abducted in Aleppo, Syria, on Thanksgiving Day 2012 and remained missing until August 2014, when a video surfaced online showing his brutal execution by ISIS extremists. On August 16, 2014, hundreds of family members, friends, and supporters gathered at Our Lady of the Holy Rosary Church in Rochester, New Hampshire, for a memorial Mass honoring James Foley — just weeks before what would have been his 41st birthday on October 18, 2014. Among them were his parents, John and Diane Foley, who had earlier unveiled a memorial stone for war correspondents in Bayeux-Calvados, France, in October 2014. Friends described Foley as a man defined by two unshakable pillars: his faith and his family. Jeremy Osgood, a close friend, said these anchors gave him 'a wealth of strength and courage.' In an emotional eulogy, Foley’s brother Mike said, 'I’ll never fully understand why Jim died — but I don’t believe he died in vain. He reminded us that good triumphs over evil. Anyone who forgot that need only follow his story.' Rev. Marc Montminy, who knew James personally, praised his dedication to giving voice to the voiceless. 'He gave his life because of it,' Montminy said. 'Jim reported from places where free speech and a free press did not exist.' Since his death, the Foley family has established the James W. Foley Legacy Fund to support journalists working in conflict zones, assist families of American hostages, and push for improved government policies in handling hostage crises.

Alizomwa miaka 40, Foley alikuwa amefungwa nchini Aleppo, Syria, mwezi wa Thanksgiving 2012 na hakutajwa tena mpaka Agosti 2014, wakati video iliyotumia kuonyesha kifo chake kwa upendo na ISIS ilipofika kwenye mtandao. Mwezi wa Agosti 16, 2014, zaidi ya mia mia mbili za watoto, wapendwa, na waponguzi walifika kwenye Kanisa la Our Lady of the Holy Rosary nchini Rochester, New Hampshire, kwa ajili ya kumbukumbu ya James Foley — mara moja kwa siku zilizopita kabla ya siku yake ya kuzaliwa ya 41, iliyokuwa tarehe 18 Oktoba 2014. Kati ya wale walio, walikuwa wazazi wake, John na Diane Foley, walioweka miongozo ya kumbukumbu ya mtaalamu wa habari nchini Bayeux-Calvados, Ufaransa, Oktoba 2014. Yeye aliyekuwa na ujuzi huo anaweza kufanya kwa kusoma historia yake.' Rev. article_content: Britain's exports to countries outside the European Union have reached a record high, as global demand continues to rise, according to official figures released yesterday. The Office for National Statistics reported that exports increased by 4.9% between April and June to a record £78.4 billion, providing a significant boost to the recovering economy. The surge in demand for goods labeled 'Made in Britain' was driven primarily by markets outside the EU, particularly in Latin America and Asia, where manufacturers have expanded operations. UK trade improved: The trade deficit—the difference between exports and imports—narrowed to £8.1 billion in June, better than the £8.5 billion forecast by economists. Over the past five years, exports to non-EU countries have grown by more than 40%, while sales to EU nations rose by just 3.1%. Exports to China, India, and Thailand have more than doubled during this period. Experts described the shift away from Europe toward faster-growing markets as 'great news for the UK economy.' Business leaders suggested this trend gives Prime Minister David Cameron leverage to demand a better deal for Britain in ongoing negotiations with Brussels over EU membership. Exports to the EU rose by 2.3% to £38.1 billion in the second quarter, but sales to non-EU countries jumped 7.5% to £40.3 billion—the first time quarterly exports to the rest of the world exceeded £40 billion. In June alone, exports to the EU fell 0.6% to £12.8 billion, while exports to non-EU markets rose 10.4% to £14.2 billion, another record. Katie Evans, an economist at the Centre for Economics and Business Research in London, said: 'Advanced economies are unlikely to return to pre-crisis growth rates, making the pivot toward emerging markets excellent news for the UK. By tapping into rapid global growth, Britain can capture a share of this new wealth.' Economist Jim O'Neill, who coined the term BRIC to describe Brazil, Russia, India, and China, said the data supports his view that the benefits of EU membership are diminishing. Trade with countries beyond the EU is seen as vital to Britain’s economic recovery, as the eurozone crisis continues to suppress demand closer to home. Matthew Elliott, CEO of Business for Britain—a campaign group advocating for renegotiated UK terms within the EU—urged the government to recognize this shift. 'With the eurozone's struggles and the rise of Asian and Latin American markets, it’s no surprise British firms are turning outward. The government must use this momentum to secure a better deal for Britain in upcoming talks with Brussels.' Although the UK’s share of global trade has declined over recent decades, manufacturers like Rolls-Royce and BAE Systems remain global leaders, contributing to the export surge. Jim O'Neill added: 'Given the dramatic realignment of global trade due to the rise of BRIC nations—especially China—neither the EU nor the eurozone remain as dominant economic blocs as they once were. The advantages of membership are no longer as compelling.' The export boom has helped shrink Britain’s trade gap. The goods trade deficit—exports minus imports—fell to £8.1 billion in June from £8.7 billion in May, well below the £8.5 billion economists had predicted. Nida Ali, economic advisor to the Ernst & Young Item Club, said: 'This confirms the strength of the UK’s economic recovery.'

Matthew Elliott, Mwenyekiti Mkuu wa Business for Britain, kikundi cha kampeni kinachosaidia kurekebisha masharti ya Uingereza katika Ulaya, aliomba serikali kuelewa huu mabadiliko. 'Kwa kuwa matatizo ya euro imepunguza uwezo wa bara, na kushinda nchi za kuanzishwa nchini Asia na Amerika ya Kusini, si kubaya kuwa wafanyabiashara wa Uingereza wamekuja kujifunza nje ya Ulaya. Serikali inapaswa kutumia mombasa huu kukuza malipo mengine mengine kwa Uingereza katika mazungumzo ya kusambaza na Brussels.' article_content: Susan Warren, known as 'The Cleaning Fairy' for tidying up strangers' homes without being asked, was arrested again after police found her shoveling snow from a driveway in Elyria, Ohio. Authorities say she was recognized by a neighbor who spotted her and reported her as suspicious. Warren, 53, was sentenced to one year of probation in November 2012 after pleading guilty to attempted burglary for entering a home in Westlake, Ohio, cleaning it, and leaving a $75 bill on a napkin for her services. On January 22, 2013, a member of the neighborhood watch noticed Warren shoveling snow and called police. Officers confirmed she was on probation and took her into custody on an outstanding warrant. Warren was not charged for the snow removal, but police noted the incident as a potential violation of her probation terms. In her previous case, Warren told investigators she drove by the house one day in May 2012 and 'wanted something to do.' She entered the home, washed dishes, vacuumed, dusted, and left a handwritten note reading, 'I was here to clean. $75.' The homeowner’s 18-year-old daughter initially believed her parents had hired a maid. Sherry Bush, the homeowner, told WKYC-TV that Warren had cleaned coffee mugs left on the counter and even left her contact information. Warren claims she operates a cleaning business and sometimes enters unoccupied homes to clean them, believing she is providing a valuable service — though she admits she does so without permission.

Wafanyakazi walipokea habari kwamba alikuwa chini ya uhakimu na kumfanya kuchukuliwa kwa sababu ya amri iliyobaki. article_content: On March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 vanished without a trace during an overnight flight from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. Despite massive international efforts, its exact location remains unknown. Radar data later suggested an unidentified aircraft veered sharply off course, heading west over the Malay Peninsula and into the Strait of Malacca — hundreds of miles from its intended route. But officials stressed this blip might not even have been MH370. China later reported satellite images showing three large floating objects, possibly debris, but confirmation has never come. One of the biggest mysteries is the sudden loss of the plane’s transponder — the device that broadcasts its identity and location to air traffic control. While it can be manually turned off, experts argue it’s extremely unlikely a pilot would do so unless under duress. Without the black boxes, investigators are left guessing: Was it sabotage? A catastrophic system failure? Or something else entirely? The search became the largest in aviation history, stretching across 27,000 miles of ocean and land, involving dozens of ships and aircraft from over a dozen nations. Volunteers worldwide tried to help by analyzing satellite photos from DigitalGlobe, overwhelming the platform with uploads. Yet the sheer scale of the search zone — remote seas, dense jungles, and mountainous terrain — made progress painfully slow. Among the passengers were two men traveling on stolen Iranian passports, but Interpol confirmed they had no ties to terrorism. Their use of fake documents was likely linked to illegal immigration or smuggling — not attack planning. Meanwhile, the pilots were seasoned professionals: Captain Zaharie Ahmad Shah had flown for over three decades; First Officer Fariq Ab Hamid was recently certified on the 777. Still, reports surfaced that Hamid once allowed passengers into the cockpit — a breach of safety norms in many countries, though not universally illegal. Mechanical failure remains a leading theory. Some analysts believe a sudden power outage could have disabled communications, leaving the crew with limited time to attempt a return to land. Others suggest a structural failure — like a ruptured window — could have rapidly depressurized the cabin, incapacitating everyone within minutes. Even the idea of a meteor strike gained fleeting attention, though experts dismissed it as implausible given the lack of physical evidence. Reports that family members’ calls to passengers’ phones continued to ring after the disappearance were widely shared. But tech experts clarified this is normal: when a phone is unreachable, the network rings for a few seconds before routing to voicemail — a delay that feels like an active line. No phone signal can survive a plane crash over open ocean. While some compare MH370 to past tragedies like Air France 447 — which took nearly two years to locate — this case stands apart. No distress call. No debris. No answers. Only questions that lingered long after the search ended.
translated_content: Mnamo 8 Machi, 2014, repudi ya Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 ilikwisha kwa uhai wakati wa safari ya usiku kutoka Kuala Lumpur hadi Beijing. Kwa mujibu wa mipango mengi ya kimataifa, mahali pa kuzama pengine hakuna kuthibitishwa. Data ya radar ilisema kuwa ndege yoyote iliyotambulika ilivyoondoka kwa mizani mingi kutoka eneo lake la awali, ikilala kaskazini mwa Penini ya Malay na kuingia katika Kisiwa cha Malacca — mizani mingi kutoka njia yake ya awali. Lakini watawala walisisitiza kuwa blip hilo bila shaka haikuwa Flight 370. China ilisema baadaye kuwa imesita picha za sateliti zinazoonyesha vitu viwili viwili vya kutosha, ikiwa ni pamoja na mengine mawili, lakini hakuna thibitisho. Moja ya mashaka makubwa ni kushuka kwa transponder ya ndege — jukumu linalotumia kutoa taarifa za kihistoria na nafasi kwa usimamizi wa hewa. Kwa nusu ya kusagwa, inaweza kuwaondolewa kwa uwezo wa mtu, lakini wataalamu wanasema ni mkubwa sana kuwa raisi atakavyoondolewa kwa sababu ya hatari. Bila kumbukumbu za kichwa na data ya ndege, watafiti wameacha kufikiri: Je, ni uongozi? Kosa la teknolojia? Au kitu kingine? Mchakato wa kupatia ndege ulikuwa mmoja kati ya makubwa zaidi katika historia ya ndege, ikilipa mizani 27,000 ya bahari na bara, na kuchukua mashine 40 na ndege 39 kutoka nchi 12. Watu wengi wa dunia walijaribu kusaidia kwa kuanalia picha za sateliti kutoka kwa DigitalGlobe, na kusababisha kushuka kwa tovuti yao. Lakini ukubwa wa eneo la kupatia — bahari mbali, mti wa kavirondo na milima — ulifanya mchakato wa kuzima kwa urahisi. Kati ya wapasa, walikuwa wawili waliofanya kwa pasipoti zilizoachwa, lakini Interpol ilithibitisha kuwa wao hawakuwa na mawasiliano na uhamasishi. Matumizi yao ya pasipoti za kibinafsi yalikuwa sawa na kuhamasa kwa njia isiyo halali au kusonga bidhaa — si mapinduzi. Kwa upande mwingine, walezi walikuwa wanaoamka: Mheshimiwa Zaharie Ahmad Shah alikuwa amefanya ndege kwa miaka 30; Mheshimiwa Fariq Ab Hamid alikuwa amekamilisha mafunzo yake kwenye Boeing 777. Lakini habari zilisema kuwa Hamid alipewa wapasa kuingia kwenye kambi ya kuchora kwa safari moja, kosa la usalama katika nchi kadhaa, lakini si kwa kila nchi. Kosa la teknolojia linakuwa miongozo mkuu. Wakati baadhi ya wataalamu wanasema kuwa kushuka kwa nguvu inaweza kuchukua mawasiliano, akilinda walezi kwa muda mfupi kufanya kurejea. Wengine wanasema kuwa kosa la mwanga — kama mlango au dirisha lililofungwa — linaweza kusababisha kushuka kwa uvuvi, na kuzima wote ndani ya sekunde chache. Hatua ya mizani ya meteor ilipata kipawa kwa muda mfupi, lakini wataalamu wamesingilia kwa sababu ya kuzuia data. Habari za kuwa simu za wapasa zilivyofanya kuchangia kwa muda mrefu baada ya kuzama zilizopatikana kwa wengi. Lakini wataalamu wa teknolojia walisema hii ni sawa: wakati simu haiwezi kupatikana, mtandao huchangia kwa dakika kadhaa kabla ya kufanya kwa simu ya barua. Kila muda huo unajulikana kama simu inayoingia, lakini kila simu haiwezi kufanya kazi baada ya kuzama kwenye bahari. Wakati baadhi ya kulinganisha Flight 370 na matukio ya awali kama Air France 447 — ambayo ilihitaji miaka 2 kuzima — hii kesi inaonekana tofauti. Haba ya kushughulikia. Mzinga. Jibu. Maswali tu ambayo yameendelea kwa muda mrefu baada ya mchakato wa kupatia kumaliza.

article_content: Desperate to boost fourth-quarter sales, stores are launching Black Friday promotions earlier than ever—some even opening on Thanksgiving Day. Several retailers began slashing prices immediately after Halloween, with Amazon leading the charge by starting its Black Friday sale a full week early, on November 21. This year, the early-morning rush to wait in line outside big-box stores may not be worth the effort. A recent WalletHub survey of over 5,500 deals found that shoppers could save more on Cyber Monday, the online sale that begins three days after Thanksgiving. Amazon is refreshing its deals throughout the week, posting new 'lightning deals' as frequently as every 10 minutes. Prime members get a 30-minute head start on these offers. Examples of discounted items include: a 32-inch Samsung TV for $247.99 (38% off), a set of Lincoln Logs for $62.66, a LeapFrog LeapBand for $24.99, a Vince Camuto handbag for $79.19 (60% off), a Canon Rebel camera for $549 ($200 off), a Dell touchscreen laptop for $659.19, and Beats headphones for $199 (59% off). Amazon is also offering 'doorbuster' deals such as a 32-inch LED TV for just $79 and a 40-inch 1080p LED TV for $119. Intel laptops are 20% off across the platform. According to WalletHub’s analysis of 22 major U.S. retailers, JCPenney offers the highest overall discounts this Black Friday at 65%, followed by Macy’s (54%), Rite Aid (53%), Meijer (51%), and Sears (50%). Walmart, Best Buy, and Costco ranked near the bottom in average discount depth, with each offering around 32% off. This may reflect their cautious approach following the 2008 Black Friday trampling death at a Walmart in Valley Stream, New York. The deepest discounts are found in specific categories: jewelry (up to 78.75% off at Kmart), apparel (69% at Sears), furniture (59.6% at Kohl’s), and consumer electronics (65.29% at Macy’s). Toys lead in volume, accounting for 26% of all Black Friday deals. Notably, Amazon did not provide complete deal data to WalletHub, meaning its true discount performance cannot be fully assessed. Other non-participating retailers include Apple, Home Depot, IKEA, and Lowe’s. Last year, Cyber Monday sales outpaced Black Friday by 10%. In 2013, average Black Friday discounts were 40%, while Cyber Monday reached 50%. Consumers may benefit from waiting, especially to confirm product availability before purchasing. The National Retail Federation projects total holiday sales (November–December) will reach $616.9 billion in 2023—a 4.1% increase from 2013’s $592.7 billion.

article_content: Inside a dilapidated warehouse, beneath scattered clothes hanging from rusty pipes, a young Black man kneels on the ground. His feet are bare, his trousers rolled to his knees as he beats his soaked shirt against the floor to remove the dirt. Nearby, a group of men stand as silent, desolate figures—some crouched washing their worn clothes, others naked, scrubbing their bodies after grueling labor. This is not a prison scene—but it might as well be. It is, instead, a communal shower room for mineworkers in apartheid-era South Africa, captured by pioneering photographer Ernest Cole over fifty years ago. A small man—barely five feet tall—with an extraordinary eye for detail, Cole was among South Africa’s first Black photojournalists. His haunting, often clandestine images revealed the daily realities of Black life under apartheid: the crushing oppression, the economic exploitation, and the dehumanizing conditions endured by his people—including mineworkers forced to live in squalor. In 1967, one year after leaving South Africa in exile, Cole published his first—and only—photo book, titled 'House of Bondage.' Banned in South Africa, the book sold out rapidly and earned widespread critical acclaim. Yet despite its impact, Cole died destitute and alone in New York in 1990, his story largely forgotten for decades. In recent years, however, Cole’s work has experienced a resurgence. Exhibitions across South Africa and internationally have reintroduced his powerful imagery to new audiences. Now, New York University’s Grey Art Gallery is hosting the first solo touring museum exhibition of 120 rare black-and-white gelatin silver prints from Cole’s archive at the Hasselblad Foundation in Gothenburg, Sweden. 'Ernest Cole’s life and work were defined by apartheid,' says Gunilla Knape, curator of the exhibition, which runs until December 6. 'It shaped his most important photographs, drove him into exile, and rendered him a stateless, yet globally recognized, stranger. This exhibition seeks to illuminate his life and make a significant portion of his archive accessible—not least to audiences in his homeland.' Born in 1940 in Eersterust, a Black freehold township near Pretoria, Cole was the fourth of six children. Raised in the countryside by an aunt to shield him from urban crime, he reunited with his parents as a teenager. At age fifteen, a family friend gave him his first camera. From then on, he carried it everywhere, documenting friends, family, and neighbors. In 1958, Cole began working as a darkroom and layout assistant at Drum Magazine, a radical Black lifestyle publication in Johannesburg. He later enrolled in a correspondence photography course from the New York Institute of Photography. By 1960, he became chief photographer for a weekly South African newspaper and a freelance contributor to international outlets. Inspired by Henri Cartier-Bresson’s unedited, candid style, Cole embarked on a dangerous mission: to expose apartheid’s injustices to the world. He worked without flash, concealed his camera in lunch bags, and even deceived authorities by reclassifying himself as 'colored'—a mixed-race designation that granted him greater mobility in restricted zones. His photographs are both subtle and searing: bulldozed townships making way for white settlements, 'Europeans Only' benches, overcrowded trains, handcuffed men arrested for lacking passes, and mineworkers subjected to humiliating medical checks. Yet he also captured joy: children playing with water cannons, friends laughing, couples dancing. 'He lived among his people,' says Knape. 'He didn’t just observe—he shared their struggles, their triumphs. He understood their world intimately.' In 1966, Cole was arrested alongside a group of street youths he had been photographing. Police offered him freedom in exchange for becoming an informant. He chose exile instead, fleeing with only the layouts for his book. Life in exile—first in Europe, then in New York—was harrowing. Homeless and isolated, he lived on the streets and subways. He died of pancreatic cancer in February 1990, just one week after Nelson Mandela’s release from prison.
translated_content: Ndani ya kienyeji cha kifupi, chini ya viti vya nguo zinazopandwa kwenye vichwao vya chuma, mwanamume mwenye ugoa wa kijiji anaanguka kwa macho yake. Miguu yake yamejaa, mavazi yake yameshikwa mpaka mkono wake kama anavyofanya kuchoma kando ya ardhi ili kupunguza ndoto. Karibu na yeye, kikundi cha wanaume wanaweza kuonekana kama wateja wa kifo—baadhi yao wamepiga kila kipande cha nguo zao za kufanya kazi, baadhi yao wamezuka bila nguo, wakiwashia mwili wao baada ya kazi ya kijeshi. Hii si taarifa ya maisha ya mapambano—lakini inaweza kuwa sawa na hiyo. Hii ni chumba cha maji ya kawaida kwa wafanyakazi wa vijivu nchini Afrika Kusini zamani, ambayo ilishtanga na mwanamfotokasi mwenye kipato, Ernest Cole, miaka miwili kumi na tano iliyopita. Mwanamume mdogo—hata kama alikuwa na kike kimoja cha miaka mitano—na kipawa cha kusema kwa maelezo, Cole alikuwa mojawapo wa wapiga picha wa kijiji wa kwanza nchini Afrika Kusini. Picha zake zilizosha na zilizokuwa kwa kibinafsi zilisaidia kueleza maisha ya kijiji kwa muda wa apartheid: utovu mkubwa, uchumi wa kuvunjika, na hali za kuzuia kibinafsi zilizotumika na watu wake—hasa wafanyakazi wa vijivu waliowekwa kwenye hali za kilele. Mnamo 1967, mwaka mmoja baada ya kufuga nchini Afrika Kusini, Cole alipatia kitabu chake cha kwanza na tu, kilichoitwa 'House of Bondage.' Kitabu hicho, ambacho kilitoa nchini Afrika Kusini, ilisukuma haraka na kupata thamani kubwa ya kihistoria. Lakini bila kujua matokeo yake, Cole alifariki kwa kipato na kifupi nchini New York mnamo 1990, na historia yake ilikuwa ikozwa kwa miaka mingi. Kwa miaka miwili iliyopita, picha za Cole zimekuwa na uchunguzi mwingine. Muziki na mazungumzo nchini Afrika Kusini na nje ya nchi zimekuwa na kuonyesha picha zake kwa wengine. Sasa, Galeri ya Grey ya Chuo Kikuu cha New York imeanza kuzingatia kazi yake ya kuanzia kwa muongozo wa kwanza wa picha 120 za mwezi wa kijiji na mwezi wa kijiji kutoka arkipeli yake ya Hasselblad Foundation nchini Gothenburg, Uswidi. 'Maisha na kazi za Ernest Cole zilikuwa zimepewa na apartheid,' anasema Gunilla Knape, mwenyekiti wa muongozo ambao unaendelea hadi Desemba 6. 'Lilo lilikuwa la kichwa cha picha zake zilizosha, lilikuwa sababu ya kufuga na kufanya yeye kuwa mtu mwenye kipato, lakini amekuwa mmoja ambaye aliuliza duniani. Muongozo huu unashughulikia kuonyesha maisha yake na kazi yake, na kutoa sehemu kubwa ya arkipeli yake kwa wengine kwa kimataifa, hasa katika nchi yake ya asili.' Alizaliwa mnamo 1940 kwenye Eersterust, mji wa kijiji wa kifupi karibu na Pretoria. Alikuwa kwanza ya kumi na sita. Alizaliwa kwenye nchi kwa mama yake ili kuzuia yeye kutoka kwa matukio ya kijeshi katika mikoa ya mji. Cole alipokea wazazi wake kama mwanamume mmoja na huo wakati mwenyewe alianza kushika kipaja. Wakati wa miaka 15, mmoja wa rafiki zake alimpa kamera yake ya kwanza. Kutoka hapo, alikuwa akipanda kamera yake mahali popote, akipiga picha za rafiki, familia, na watu wengine. Mnamo 1958, Cole alianza kufanya kazi kama msaidizi wa chumba cha kifua na kipengele cha Drum Magazine, chuo cha kijiji cha kijeshi cha Johannesburg. Akashiriki kwa mkataba wa kipaja kutoka New York Institute of Photography kabla ya kufuga kwa Drum mnamo 1960 ili kufanya kazi kama mwanamfotokasi mkuu wa gazeti la kisiku la Afrika Kusini na kwa kampuni za kimataifa. Kwa kusudi na kipaja cha Henri Cartier-Bresson, ambaye hakuwa akikatiza picha zake, Cole alianza kazi ya hatari: kuchukulia utovu wa apartheid na kutoa kwa watu nje ya Afrika Kusini. Aliwahi kufanya kazi bila flash, akishikia kamera yake ndani ya vitu vya chakula, na hata kudai kuwa alikuwa mtoto mwenye kipato ili kuhakikisha kuwa amepewa mazingira ya kijiji kwa ajili ya kusafirisha. Picha zake zinaweza kuwa zilizosha na zilizokuwa na kipaja: mikoa ya kijiji zilizochomwa ili kufanya miji ya wazungu, benchi zinazoonyesha 'Wazungu tu,' treni zilizopakuliwa, wanaume wamevishwa na makosa ya kuchukua kwa kushika kifungu, na wafanyakazi wa vijivu waliowekwa kwenye masikio ya kizuia kibinafsi. Lakini alipiga picha zilizosha pia: watoto wanaofanya kazi na maji, rafiki wanaogharisha, na mke na mwanamme wanaopiga picha. 'Alikuwa amefanya kazi na watu wake,' anasema Knape. 'Hakuwa akiondoa tu—alikuwa akishirikiana na matukio yao, mapenzi yao, na yote. Alikuwa akijua kwa makini nini ilikuwa kiko karibu.' Mnamo 1966, Cole alikaa na kikundi cha watoto wa kijiji ambao walikuwa amepigia picha. Polisi walimwambia kuwa alitaka kuwa mtaalamu ili kuepuka kufungwa. Cole aliamua kufuga nchini Afrika Kusini, akishirikiana na kipengele cha kitabu chake. Maisha ya kufuga—kwanza nchini Ulaya, baadaye nchini Marekani—ilikuwa duni. Aliishi kwenye mitaa na metro ya New York. Alifariki kwa saratani ya kibuni mnamo Februari 1990, wiki moja baada ya kufungwa kwa Nelson Mandela.

article_content: In New York City, multiple CitiBike docking stations have been removed or relocated following complaints from wealthy residents who deemed them unsightly or inconvenient. Since their debut on Memorial Day, at least ten stations have been taken down — including one outside the West Soho co-op of actor John Slattery, star of 'Mad Men'. According to The New York Post, some removals followed formal legal threats or neighborhood petitions, while others occurred after simple phone calls from influential residents. For instance, a station near the IAC Building in Chelsea — designed by famed architect Frank Gehry — was moved across the street after management raised concerns, though insiders suggested the real issue was disruption to luxury events hosted by CEO Barry Diller. Meanwhile, community groups and street vendors in other neighborhoods have struggled to gain similar leverage. A 40-bike station installed at Liberty Street and Broadway displaced five food carts, yet efforts to relocate it failed despite organized protests. 'They ignored us, basically,' said Sean Basinski of the Street Vendor Project. Attorney Jim Walden criticized the disparity, noting that the city seemed willing to accommodate affluent property owners while disregarding low-income advocates. He is currently seeking to remove a station from Petrosino Square in Soho, backed by 600 signatures and 132 letters — yet the station remains. Another case involved a proposed station near Frank's Bike Shop on the Lower East Side. Despite a petition signed by 1,000 locals warning it would hurt business, the city refused to budge. In contrast, attorney Steven Sladkus successfully pressured the DOT to move a 29-bike station from the Milan Condominium on East 55th Street, where units sell for up to $3.7 million — a building also used as a filming location for 'The Wolf of Wall Street'. Sladkus quipped that no CitiBike station would ever appear in front of Mayor Bloomberg’s townhouse, suggesting a double standard: 'Maybe the same courtesy should have been given to all other property owners in the city.' The Department of Transportation declined to comment on these allegations.

Kwa mujibu wa The New York Post, baadhi ya kutoa mashine ilifanyika baada ya makundi ya hukumu au ombi la kijiji, lakini baadhi yengine zilipunguzwa baada ya simu tu kutoka wakazi wenye nishati. Kwa mfano, mashine moja karibu na Mkono wa IAC katika Chelsea — iliyoundwa na mvulana wa kisasa Frank Gehry — ilibadilishwa kushoto mtaa baada ya uongozi kuwasiliana na changamoto, lakini wapimbo walianza kuwa tatizo ni kuzungumza vipindi vya kina vya CEO Barry Diller. Mashine ya 40 ya CitiBike iliyofunguliwa kwenye Liberty Street na Broadway iligawanya vitanda vya chakula viwili, lakini jaribio la kubadilisha mashine hayo haikufanikiwa bila mapambano yaliyofanyika. 'Wamekataa wetu, kwa mujibu wa kawaida,' alisema Sean Basinski kutoka kwa Street Vendor Project. Amejaribu kutoa mashine moja nje ya Petrosino Square katika Soho, na kusaidiwa na hati 600 na barua 132 — lakini mashine haijapunguzwa. Mfano mwingine ulikuwa mashine ya CitiBike iliyopendekezwa karibu na Frank's Bike Shop katika Lower East Side. Kwa upande wa 1000 watu walioandika ombi kuwa mashine itasababisha uzembe wa biashara, serikali haikubali kubadilisha. Serikali ya Uendeshaji wa Barabarani haikujibu maswali haya.

article_content: This is the moment a woman slapped an assistant of Julien Blanc, a controversial pick-up artist, as tensions escalated following the cancellation of one of his seminars in Melbourne. The incident occurred just hours before Blanc was deported from Australia after Immigration Minister Scott Morrison revoked his visa over what were described as 'abhorrent views' toward women. Footage uploaded to YouTube shows an angry woman confronting Blanc’s assistant, known only as RSD Max, as a crowd chanted, 'Sexual assault is not OK.' The woman, identifiable by her green dreadlocks, struck RSD Max across the face before being pulled away by a bystander. A separate video, posted by the YouTube channel Support RSD (Real Social Dynamics), captures a large group of protesters confronting RSD Max. One female protester verbally abused him before slapping him. Blanc, who previously boasted about his choking technique making him appear like a 'rock star celebrity' with a 'f***ing attractive, magnetic personality,' and who encouraged followers to emulate comedian Russell Brand, was forced to leave Australia on Thursday. Morrison stated, 'This guy wasn't pushing forward political ideas—he was promoting views derogatory to women, and that's something our values abhor in this country.' Blanc had planned to host a seminar aboard a boat along Southbank in Melbourne, but Melbourne River Cruises canceled the event after a large crowd of demonstrators gathered and demanded its shutdown. His deportation followed a sustained social media campaign under the hashtag #TakeDownJulienBlanc.

article_content: In the mid-1990s, a Frenchman named Frederic Bourdin walked into the lives of a grieving Texas family and convinced them he was their long-missing 16-year-old son, Nicholas Barclay. The catch? Bourdin was 23, had brown eyes instead of blue, and bore little resemblance to the boy they’d lost three years prior. Yet, over five months, he lived with them—dyeing his hair blond, faking a tattoo with a pen, and weaving a heartbreaking story about abuse and medical experiments by captors. It wasn’t until a private investigator dug deeper that the truth surfaced. Bourdin wasn’t just a one-time fraudster. Over nearly two decades, he assumed more than 40 identities across Europe, always portraying a lost child. He was caught impersonating a Spanish orphan in France in 2005, and before that, a missing 14-year-old from Isère in 2003—all uncovered eventually by DNA tests or surveillance. Born in 1974 near Paris, Bourdin was abandoned by his mother at age two and raised by impoverished grandparents. By 12, he was in a juvenile facility. His earliest attempt to pass as a British child failed because he couldn’t speak English. From there, he learned languages, studied human behavior, and turned impersonation into a way to survive—and to feel loved. After serving six years in prison, he didn’t stop. He married a Frenchwoman in 2007, had three children, and even consulted on a film about his life, 'The Chameleon,' where he was portrayed by Canadian actor Marc-André Grondin. Though labeled a con artist, Bourdin himself said he simply wanted to belong. The real mystery isn’t how he fooled people—it’s why so many were willing to believe him.

Kwa nini? Bourdin alikuwa na miaka 23, pumzi zake zilikuwa za kahawia bila kuhesabiwa kushika kifungu cha bluu, na hakuna mshale wowote wa kujulikana na mtoto ambaye waliohisi. Lakini kwa muda wa masaa miwili, alikuwa ameishi na wao—kupiga nywele zake kwa rangi ya bluu, kufanya mkono kwa kisasi, na kuzingatia historia ya kibaya kuhusu mapenzi na matukio ya kimsingi na viongozi wake. Hakutajwa kwa ajili ya mtafiti wa kibinafsi ambaye alipata ujuzi. Bourdin hakuwa mmoja tu wa wazalishaji. Kwa karibu miaka elfu mbili, alitumia zaidi ya 40 jina, daima kuchukua utu wa mtoto mchanga. Alipotazama kwa kuwa mwanafunzi mchanga wa Hispania nchini Ufaransa mwaka 2005, na kabla hayo, mtoto wa miaka 14 ambaye alikufa nchini Isère mwaka 2003—zote zimefanywa kwa matumizi ya DNA au kuchunguza. Alizaliwa mwaka 1974 karibu na Paris, Bourdin alikosa mama yake kwa miaka mbili na kuwa na makaburi ya kijiji. Kwa miaka 12, alikuwa katika shule ya watoto wasio na usalama. Kuanzia huko, alisomea lugha, kujifunza tabia ya binadamu, na kubadilisha kujitokeza kama njia ya kuzuia na kushiriki. Baada ya kupigwa kwa miaka sita, hakukufa. Alihamasisha mke wa Faransa mwaka 2007, aliweza watoto wawili, na pia alikuwa mshauri kwenye filamu ya maisha yake, 'The Chameleon,' ambayo alivyoonyeshwa na mwigizaji wa Kanada Marc-André Grondin. Hata kwa kuwa amekuwa mwanachama wa kufanya kazi, Bourdin alisema kwamba alitaka tu kuwa sehemu. Sera ya kubuni si jinsi alivyofanya watu—ni kwa nini watu wengi walikuwa wamepewa kuzingatia.

article_content: Football Manager 2015 is getting a major upgrade — 15-year-old Norwegian sensation Martin Odegaard is officially joining the game. His father, Hans Erik Odegaard, who works as assistant manager at Mjondalen, personally gave Sports Interactive the green light. Although the game typically excludes players under 16, Hans Erik’s handwritten note changed everything: 'I hereby grant you permission to add Martin Odegaard to Football Manager 2015. Best wishes,' it read. Studio director Miles Jacobson shared a photo of the note on Twitter, confirming the addition. Martin, an attacking midfielder for Stromsgodset, has already drawn attention from Europe’s biggest clubs — including Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, and Bayern Munich. But despite all those offers, the teen is a die-hard Liverpool supporter. Before Christmas, he’ll head to Anfield for a trial, following a previous stint with Real Madrid. With his technical brilliance and composure beyond his years, Odegaard is poised to become one of the most exciting young talents ever featured in the FM series.

article_content: 'Take deep breaths,' I tell my son. The irony of the instruction isn't lost on me after he begins to explain why he's so upset. It's the end of a long day — dark well before I think it should be, as the cold hasn't quite taken full hold in Atlanta. I received the text from Dr. Adams just before 3 p.m. Once my abnormal psychology professor, now a respected colleague in the department, her message read: 'No indictment... disbelieving.' I had come to terms with this injustice visited upon Eric Garner and others — at least in my mind. I'd compartmentalized things since the week before, following the no-indictment decision in Ferguson, Missouri. I clinically carried on with lecturing and working with my students from Spelman and Morehouse, helping them process their protest of solidarity with Ferguson and the epidemic of extrajudicial killings of Black people. They launched their 'Make It Matter' protest last Tuesday at the foot of the Martin Luther King statue on Morehouse's campus and marched to the CNN Center a few miles away. I was proud. Teary-eyed. They lifted me up. I'd brought my son to work that day. And that's when I began a focused dialogue with him — in 7-year-old terms — about Ferguson, Michael Brown, and issues of race and social justice. The little guy took it well, asked a few clarifying questions, and then concluded, 'But if a police officer is supposed to protect people and then shoots a teenager because he's afraid of him — even though the teenager doesn't have a gun — then the police officer is a brute.' Exactly. Since then, I've talked with, taught, and consoled students on campus, reflecting on the turmoil I experienced some 22 years ago after the police beating of Rodney King. Eric Garner's killing is an amplified, 21st-century manifestation of that violence, echoing past New York cases like those of Yusuf Hawkins, Michael Griffith, and William Turks. Still, I've resisted putting it all together. Donovan X. Ramsey explained it so well last month in his essay 'Without Sanctuary.' But then my son, voice trembling after a long day, said, 'I've been thinking about the problems in the world.' Wow. I knew he seemed unfazed last week. 'And Mike Brown... and people don't like other people because of their skin,' he continued, before collapsing between the front and back seats, sobbing into my arms. 'Breathe,' I said, using every ounce of strength I have not to cry with him — not right now. He doesn't even know about the failure to indict Officer Pantaleo in New York on Tuesday. 'The world is better already because of people like you,' I said, trying to reframe the conversation. 'You know what's right and what's wrong, and so do the students you met last week. And we're all going to be kind to one another, study hard, and figure out how to make it better.' I sounded convincing — as parents are supposed to. The academic year began with the police killings of Michael Brown and Eric Garner, and it ends with the decision that these deaths were somehow legal. That weighs heavily on so many. In the bubble we build at Morehouse College, we uplift young Black men. We strive to show them the best parts of who they are, making visible a humanity that the broader society refuses to recognize as normal. That's the core of our work. But it's a hard sell when the young people you're trying to reason with point out that you can be shot to death in broad daylight or choked to death on camera simply because white people are afraid of you. Still, the truth is that Black men, women, and children — girls and boys — are not disposable. We are valuable. We are not objects. Breathe. Of course, this is as much a mantra for me as it is instruction to my son. Breathe — and then let's keep doing the work.

article_content: In London, shopping isn’t just a pastime—it’s a cultural ritual, especially during the January sales. Every year, the city’s bustling streets fill with eager shoppers, from locals hunting for discounts to international visitors drawn by exclusive deals. Among these global shoppers, one nation has quietly risen to prominence: Nigeria. Once overshadowed by traditional high-spend markets like China and the Middle East, Nigerian consumers are now making waves in London’s luxury retail scene. According to Sue West of Selfridges, Nigeria’s spending power has surged over the past year and a half, becoming a key driver of international sales. While Chinese and Middle Eastern tourists remain dominant, Nigeria’s growth is unmistakable—and intentional. The reasons behind this shift are rooted in Nigeria’s evolving economy. Despite nearly two-thirds of its population living on less than $1 a day, a small but rapidly expanding affluent class has emerged, fueled by gains in telecom, finance, and entrepreneurship—not just oil. These new consumers are traveling more, flying direct to London on increasingly frequent flights, and taking advantage of perks like British Airways’ 23kg free baggage allowance. Retailers haven’t missed the signal. Selfridges has partnered with Lagos-based fashion house Style House Files to launch an in-store showcase featuring Nigerian designers—a move designed to resonate deeply with Nigerian shoppers seeking homegrown elegance alongside global luxury brands. Omoyemi Akerele, Style House Files’ director, calls it a dream come true for local talent and a smart branding win for Selfridges, strengthening loyalty among African customers. Data backs the trend: Nigerian tourists spent an average of £107 daily in the UK in 2011, and tax-free spending from Nigeria jumped 11% year-on-year between January and September of last year. For many Nigerians, a trip to London isn’t just vacation—it’s an opportunity to access products unavailable at home, from designer labels to unique artisanal goods. As Nigeria’s middle class grows, so does its global consumer footprint—rewriting the story of African spending power, one shopping bag at a time.

Kwa kusema na Sue West kutoka Selfridges, uwezo wa kununua wa Nigeria umekua sana katika miaka miwili iliyopita, kuwa sababu muhimu ya biashara za nje. Wengine wanaoendelea kuwa na matokeo mengi ni Wachina na Washariki, lakini uongezeo wa Nigeria ni wazi na kwa sababu. Sababu za kuchukua hii mabadiliko ni kwenye uuguzi wa Nigeria. Wateja hawa wanaenda zaidi, kupelekwa kwa ndege zinazofanya safari kwa muda mrefu kwa Londini, na kuchukua faida ya mafanikio ya British Airways ya kutoa 23kg ya malighafi bila ada. Wauzaji hawajapata kushindwa. Selfridges ameongeza pamoja na mkataba wa fasheni la Lagos, Style House Files, ili kuundisha mchoro wa ndani ambapo mbinu za mwanamke wa Nigeria zinaweza kuonyesha kazi zao nje ya Afrika ya Magharibi. Wakati jamii ya kati ya Nigeria inazidi, kipato chake cha kibiashara kinazidi—kupakua historia ya uwezo wa kununua wa Afrika, kwa kichwa moja kwa kichwa.

article_content: Less than a year before hosting the World Cup, Brazil is once again in the news for the wrong reasons. On Wednesday, Brazilian football players staged a protest, saying they might take further action — possibly 'drastic measures' — if their confederation does not address the country’s overcrowded match schedule. They are demanding more vacation time, longer preseasons, fewer games, and greater input in decision-making. In several matches, players crossed their arms before or after the opening whistle. In some cases, they passed the ball end-to-end after referees threatened to issue yellow cards. In one match, players from both teams unfurled a banner in the center of the pitch during the national anthem. It read: 'For a football that is better for everyone.' In a Facebook statement, Common Sense F.C. — not a club but a player-led movement advocating for reform — wrote: 'If there are attempts to prevent players from expressing themselves peacefully, drastic measures will be taken. We expect an official response and concrete actions that benefit Brazilian football.' According to Brazilian media, possible future actions include extending arm-crossing protests, wearing red clown noses, or even stopping games. No official response was issued on Friday, a national holiday in Brazil. The protests come two weeks after a former professional footballer was found decapitated in Rio de Janeiro.

Wanaomba muda zaidi ya kusali, muda mrefu wa kuanza kwa mchezo, mchezo chache zaidi, na nafasi zaidi katika kushiriki kwa uamuzi. Katika baadhi ya michezo, wachezaji walikata mkono wao kabla au baada ya upiga kikombe. Katika baadhi ya mifumo, wamepasa mbio kutoka kwenye moja hadi nyingine baada ya hakimishe wakasema watapea kadi nyekundu. Tuna tazama majibu ya rasmi na hatua zinazotaka kusaidia mpira wa miguu wa Brazil.' article_content: During the 2014 Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford, Wigan Warriors’ Ben Flower shocked the rugby world with a brutal two-punch assault on St Helens’ Lance Hohaia — first knocking him unconscious, then delivering a second strike while he lay motionless on the ground. In a heartfelt apology, Flower admitted there was no excuse for his actions, describing it as a moment of uncontrollable emotion during a fiercely contested derby. 'I instantly regretted it,' he said, adding that he had never intended to hurt another player and was devastated to have betrayed the values of his club and the sport. Though Hohaia, who was injured and removed from the field, later expressed forgiveness and urged others to move on, the incident became the defining moment of a match otherwise remembered for St Helens’ hard-fought 14-6 victory. The Rugby Football League swiftly announced plans to convene an independent disciplinary panel led by High Court Judge Chris Batty, with Flower facing the possibility of a lifetime ban. Even though both Hohaia and St Helens’ coaching staff opposed criminal proceedings, police are still evaluating whether charges should be pursued. Media outlets like the BBC refused to rebroadcast the clip, citing its extreme violence. While teammates rallied around Flower, calling him passionate but flawed, commentators lamented how one act of rage erased a milestone moment for rugby league — a rare chance to capture mainstream attention during an international weekend. Many fear the punch will become the lasting symbol of the 2014 season, undermining years of progress in promoting the sport’s integrity.

Katika maoni yake ya kuheshimu, Flower alisema hakuna upinzani kwa mapambano yake, akichukulia kuwa yalikuwa muda wa kivivu na mafanikio ya kushindana katika mchezo unaofanana na ujasiri. 'Nimekosa kila kitu,' alisema, akiongeza kwamba hakuna nia yake ya kumchukua mchezaji mwingine na kumeza kwa sababu alikuwa amechoka na kuzingatia thamani za klabu yake na michezo. Hohaia, ambaye alipata tiba na kuondolewa, alisema baadaye kuwa amekuwa na upendo na kupendekeza wengine kufanya kazi na kusimama. Lakini matokeo ya mchakato ulikuwa miongoni mwa michezo ambayo ilikuwa imeumbwa kwa mapambano ya 14-6 ya St Helens. Kanda ya Rugbi ya Uingereza iliamua kuchukua hatua za kikatiba na kukuza kikao cha kibinafsi chenye Mhukumu wa Kupanga Chris Batty, ambapo Flower anaweza kupewa kati ya kuzuia kwa miaka mingi. Hata hivyo, Hohaia na timu ya St Helens walihodhi kuwa hazitakiwi kushughulikia kiasi cha kriminali, lakini polisi bado wanatazama ikiwa kosa la kriminali litaendelea. Wakati wengine kama BBC walikataa kuzingatia video, kwa sababu ya ujasiri wake kali. Wageni wa Wigan walikubaliana na Flower, akisema alikuwa mwenye upendo na kushindwa, lakini wanasayansi walijibu kwa kusema kuwa mmoja wa mapambano haya yamekuwa miongoni mwa michezo ya 2014, na kuchangia kusimama kwa miaka mingi ya kuboresha uhuru wa michezo.

article_content: Dafydd Raw-Rees, the 64-year-old owner of Welsh meat processor Farmbox Meats, lives a life of luxury — often seen vacationing on yachts and attending elite events like the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix and the Chequered Flag Ball, where he was photographed alongside celebrities such as Leona Lewis. Despite this opulent image, his business is now at the center of a major food scandal involving horse meat contamination. The Food Standards Agency ordered Farmbox to halt operations after allegations surfaced that it processed meat from Peter Boddy’s slaughterhouse in West Yorkshire, which was then mixed into beef products sold across Europe. Raw-Rees strongly denies any intentional fraud, stating he purchased the meat in good faith and was unaware of its true origin. He told the Sun newspaper that only 15 pallets were ever received, and they were rejected after inspection. He insists Farmbox does not produce minced meat or burgers and that all processed goods were shipped to Belgium, never entering the UK market. Although officially shut down by regulators, reports indicate the facility remained active. Raw-Rees, who resides in a large home near the plant with his wife Sarah-Jane and daughter Rhian, called the accusations 'baffling and ruinous,' saying he merely performs cutting services and has no control over what happens to the meat afterward.

Hata hivyo, biashara yake sasa iko katika kitufe cha fahamizo la nyama ya farasi. Agency ya Maisha ya Chakula iliamua kufungua Farmbox baada ya mapendekezo ya kuwa imefanya nyama kutoka kwenye mradi wa Peter Boddy nchini West Yorkshire, ambayo ilikuwa imefungwa katika bidhaa za nyama ya ng'ombe zinazotumika nchini Ulaya. article_content: Susie Dent turned 50 last year, despite numerous interviews and online biographies incorrectly stating she is 47. Known as the queen of Dictionary Corner on the long-running words-and-numbers quiz show Countdown, she has been a fixture on the program for over three decades. Although her official birth year is 1964 — confirmed by school records and a birth certificate — many sources, including the Internet Movie Database (IMDb), list her birthdate as September 21, 1967, making her appear three years younger. In a June 2023 interview, her age was mistakenly reported as 46, aligning with the incorrect IMDb listing. However, a 2005 article by her former Countdown colleague Carol Vorderman correctly identified her as 41 at the time. Online forums, particularly Wikipedia discussion pages, have turned her age into a running joke, with users joking, 'As an angel, Susie Dent has no date of birth.' The truth was eventually uncovered by fans who cross-referenced sources, including a classmate from the Marist Convent in Sunninghill who recalled they were both born in 1964. Susie Dent, born in Woking, Surrey, to Malcolm and Shirley Dent, attended private school and now lives in Oxford with her partner, Paul Atkins, and their two daughters, Lucy (15) and Thea (7). She first appeared on Countdown in 1992 at age 27 and has since appeared in nearly 2,500 episodes, taking only brief breaks for illness and maternity leave. Her role involves providing solutions to the show’s anagram puzzles — a task occasionally aided by producers via an earpiece, as revealed in 2009. A representative for Miss Dent declined to comment further but noted, 'I imagine she celebrates her birthday every year with her family.'
translated_content: Susie Dent alikuwa na miaka 50 mwaka uliopita, lakini mara nyingi maelezo kwenye mitandao na machapisho yaliyotaja kuwa ameza miaka 47. Anajulikana kama mfalme wa Dictionary Corner kwenye show ya kucheza maneno na nambari ya Countdown, ambayo amefanya kazi kwa muda mrefu zaidi ya miaka 30. Hata hivyo, mwaka wake wa kuzaliwa ni 1964 — iliyosahihishwa na rekodi za shule na hati ya kuzaliwa — lakini madarakani mengi, ikiwa ni pamoja na Internet Movie Database (IMDb), yanaonyesha tarehe ya kuzaliwa yake kama Septemba 21, 1967, kusababisha kuonekana kuwa ameza miaka 3 chini. Katika mazungumzo ya Juni 2023, umri wake uliwekwa kama 46, ambayo inaongeza na rekodi ya IMDb. Lakini makala ya 2005 na mshiriki wake wa Countdown, Carol Vorderman, iliyofanya kazi kwa furaha ya kuwa mwanamke katika miaka 40, iliyosema kwamba alikuwa na miaka 41 wakati huo. Forum za mtandao, hasa vikwazo vya Wikipedia, vimekuwa na ujumbe wa kucheza kuhusu umri wake, na watumiaji wanakusema, 'Kama malaika, Susie Dent hana tarehe ya kuzaliwa.' Ukweli uliwekwa kwa ajili ya wapenzi walioshawishi kwa kuchambua vyombo vingine, ikiwa ni pamoja na mwanafunzi wa Shule ya Marist Convent, Sunninghill, ambaye alisema wao wote walizaliwa 1964. Susie Dent, aliyezaliwa Woking, Surrey, kwa Malcolm na Shirley Dent, alifanya elimu ya kibinafsi na sasa anaishi Oxford na mke wake, Paul Atkins, na watoto wawili, Lucy (15) na Thea (7). Alianza kufanya kazi kwenye Countdown mwaka 1992 kwa umri wa 27 na tangu hiyo ameonesha katika karibu 2,500 epizodi, akishughulikia mapema tu kwa ajili ya magonjwa na mafuriko ya kuzaliwa. Kazi yake ni kutoa majibu ya vipande vya Countdown — kazi ambayo mara nyingi inasaidiwa na wawekezaji kupitia kikombe cha kila. Hii ilisajiliwa mwaka 2009. Mtu mmoja wa mamlaka ya Miss Dent hakukubaliana kumtaja zaidi lakini alisema, 'Ninadhani anaimba tarehe yake kila mwaka na familia yake.'
post_content: Susie Dent is 50 🎉 But guess what? IMDb says she’s 47 😅 Turns out, she’s been quietly celebrating for years — and we’re all just catching up! #CountdownQueen #SusieDent #AgeIsJustANumber #DictionaryCorner

article_content: On a quiet hike in Banff National Park, Minnesota couple Melissa and Jackson Brandts were setting up a wireless selfie when an unexpected guest stole the spotlight — a curious little squirrel. As they fiddled with their camera remote, the rodent darted in and out of frame, seemingly drawn by the click of the shutter. One snap caught it mid-glance, wide-eyed and perfectly focused, while the humans blurred behind it in laughter. What started as a playful moment turned into a global phenomenon. After submitting the image to National Geographic’s 'Your Shot' contest, the photo landed on the cover of the magazine’s November issue and exploded across the internet. Suddenly, 'Crasher Squirrel' had a Wikipedia page, a Twitter account, and a Facebook fan club with over five thousand followers. The park itself began using the image in promotional materials, and websites popped up letting people paste the squirrel into famous historical photos — from the moon landing to D-Day. Even Melissa’s husband started seeing the squirrel appear in coworkers’ PowerPoint presentations. When hosts like Matt Lauer questioned whether the photo was fake, the Brandts stood firm: it was real. National Geographic verified it using the original high-res file. 'You can’t make this stuff up,' Melissa said. And honestly? No one would’ve believed it if they hadn’t seen it themselves.
translated_content: Kwa mkutano wa kawaida katika Baraza la Banff, mke na mume kutoka Minnesota, Melissa na Jackson Brandts walijaribu kufanya picha yao ya selfie kupitia remote wakati mchungaji mmoja alifika kwa muda wa kipya — mchungaji mdogo mwenye furaha. Wakati walivyo kushughulikia kamera yao, mchungaji alifika na kuchukua nafasi kwa njia ambayo ilikuwa inaonekana kuwa amekuwa amepewa kikomo cha kamera. Picha moja iliamua kuona yeye kwa muda mrefu, kwa macho mengi na kwa uangalifu, wakati wale wengine walikuwa wamefanywa blur na kucheza. Mwisho ulioanza kama momenti ya kibinafsi iliabadilishwa kuwa fenomeni ya duniani. Baada ya kutoa picha kwenye versi ya 'Your Shot' ya National Geographic, picha ile ilipata nafasi ya kushtaka katika chini cha maandishi ya November na ikawa viongozi ya mtandaoni. Kwa haraka, 'Crasher Squirrel' alikuwa na ukurasa wa Wikipedia, akaunti ya Twitter, na kikundi cha Facebook kilichokuwa na zaidi ya elfu tano na mia tatu wa wapendelezi. Baraza lake lilitumia picha hiyo katika matangazo yake, na vikundi vingine vilivyofunguliwa kutoa mchungaji kwenye picha za historia — kutoka kwenye kifo cha D-Day hadi kwenye kupiga mwanga kwenye mwezi. Hata mume wa Melissa alianza kuona mchungaji akifika katika msingi ya kazi yake. article_content: The Royal Bank of Scotland is under investigation for allegedly undermining small businesses to profit from their collapse. The Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is reviewing allegations that RBS intentionally pushed viable companies into its Global Restructuring Group (GRG) by encouraging minor loan violations. Once inside GRG, these businesses reportedly faced punitive fees and interest rates, leading to financial ruin — allowing RBS to acquire their assets at deeply discounted prices. The claims stem from a critical report by Lawrence Tomlinson, appointed as entrepreneur-in-residence by the Department for Business. UK Business Secretary Vince Cable called the findings 'appalling,' while Chancellor George Osborne labeled them 'shocking.' Although the SFO has not yet launched a formal probe, it is actively assessing whether RBS’s conduct crossed from unethical into illegal territory. Separately, data from Sir Andrew Large, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, shows RBS’s lending to small businesses plummeted by £17 billion since its 2008 taxpayer-funded rescue — falling from £55 billion to £38 billion. In response, both the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority have initiated reviews, and RBS itself has hired the law firm Clifford Chance to conduct an internal audit.

article_content: For over 20 years, Zena Williams kept a painful secret: she had been pulling out her own hair since she was 11. What started as an unconscious habit during a quiet moment in class spiraled into a lifelong struggle with trichotillomania—a psychological condition where people compulsively pull their hair, often without realizing it. To avoid judgment, she told everyone she had alopecia, an autoimmune disorder that causes hair loss. The lie felt safer than explaining something no one understood. When she returned to school wearing a wig to cover bald patches from summer-long pulling, the teasing began. Classmates mocked her with nicknames like 'cancer face,' convinced her hair loss was due to chemotherapy. Her mother, struggling financially, spent their last £50 on a wig that didn’t fool anyone—but it protected Zena from being bullied for being bald. Instead, she was tormented for wearing it. The emotional toll was crushing. Zena became withdrawn, struggled to form lasting relationships, and battled depression. Even when she briefly grew back some hair, she resorted to cutting herself with scissors to cope with the urge to pull. Pregnancy offered a rare reprieve: overwhelmed by nausea, she forgot to pull—and for the first time since childhood, she had a full head of hair when her daughter Amy was born. It wasn’t until she stumbled upon a YouTube video of another young woman with trichotillomania that Zena realized her experience had a name—and that she wasn’t alone. Tears streamed down her face. 'I thought I was the only one doing something so disgusting,' she said. Since then, she’s confided in close friends and joined online support groups, finding solace in shared stories. Today, at 32, Zena still lives with the physical scars: permanent bald spots on her scalp that won’t regrow. She dyes her skin and scalp black and always styles her hair tightly pulled back. She hasn’t pulled from her head in two years—but still pulls from her arms and legs as a stress outlet. 'People say, “Just stop,”' she explains. 'But it’s not a choice. It’s like trying to stop breathing when you’re anxious.' Now on a waiting list for cognitive behavioral therapy, Zena hopes treatment will help her break free—not just for herself, but for Amy. She avoids swimming pools, fears revealing her scalp, and dreams of feeling beautiful enough to hug her daughter without hiding. 'I want her to grow up thinking hair is normal—not something to be ashamed of.'

Kwa kuzuia maoni, alisema kila mtu ameboreshwa kuwa na alopecia, hali ya kimwili ambayo inasababisha kushuka kwa nyuso. Siri hiyo ilikuwa rahisi kuliko kueleza kitu ambacho hakuna mtu akijua. Mchezo wa kuzaliwa ulikuwa na muda mwingine wa kupumzika: kwa sababu ya uchovu, aliweka kipato chake kwa muda—na kwa mara ya kwanza kutoka umri wa 11, alikuwa na nyuso zote zake zilizokuwa zimepita kwa kuzaliwa kwa mtoto wake Amy. Hakuna muda wa kuchukua video ya YouTube ya mwanamke mdogo mmoja ambaye alikuwa na trichotillomania, Zena ilikuwa na kujua kuwa kipato chake kilikuwa na jina—na kuwa hakuna mmoja tu. Macho yake yalikuwa na maji. 'Nilijua nilikuwa mmoja tu anayefanya kitu kali sana,' alisema. Ulimwengu wangu unapokea wenzangu na kujisaidia kwenye kikundi cha kijamii, kwa kuona historia za wengine. Leo, umri wake ni 32, Zena bado anaishi na viumbe vya kiufundi: sehemu nyingi za kifo zinazozidi kurejea. Akipima nguo na kigogo chake kwa rangi nyekundu, na daima kufanya nyuso zake zikikatika kwa kipya. Ameshindwa kushuka nyuso zake kwa miaka miwili—lakini bado anashuka nyuso za mkono na miguu kama kipato cha kuzungumza. 'Watu husema, “Chukua,”' alisema. 'Lakini si chaguo. Ni kama kushindwa kufa wakati unaishi kwa ajili ya kizuizi.' Sasa ameandaliwa kwenye orodha ya kusubiri kwa ujumbe wa terapia ya kibinafsi, Zena inatamani kuwa na matibabo ambayo itasaidia kushinda—si kwa ajili yake tu, bali kwa ajili ya Amy. Amevuta kuchemsha maji, anasimama na kufanya kichwa chake, na akisikia kuzaliwa kwa mtoto wake bila kuchukua kigogo. 'Nataka yeye aweze kukuza kwa kujua kuwa nyuso ni kawaida—si kitu cha kuchukua kipato.'

article_content: Mark Zuckerberg reportedly expressed strong disapproval of Twitter, calling it 'such a mess, it’s as if they drove a clown car into a gold mine and fell in,' according to Nick Bilton’s book Hatching Twitter: A True Story of Money, Power, Friendship, and Betrayal. The comment, made within the past three years, allegedly followed two failed attempts by Zuckerberg to acquire the social network — including direct outreach to co-founder Jack Dorsey. Twitter went public on the New York Stock Exchange last Thursday, opening to a roaring debut with a 72.69% surge in its first day of trading, closing at nearly $43. However, shares dipped 7.26% the next day to $41.64 as investor enthusiasm cooled slightly. Unlike Facebook’s troubled 2012 IPO — where shares priced at $38 quickly plunged below that level, taking over a year to recover — Twitter deliberately set its IPO price lower at $26. This cautious move allowed for significant post-listing gains, avoiding the perception of overvaluation. While underwriters had suggested pricing as high as $28, Twitter opted to leave room for market momentum. As a result, the company raised $1.8 billion, leaving over $1 billion in potential additional revenue on the table — a strategic trade-off deemed worth it to ensure stability. Twitter CFO Anthony Noto emphasized learning from Facebook’s missteps, prioritizing long-term confidence over short-term fundraising maximization.

Mwongozo huo, uliowekwa ndani ya miaka mitatu iliyopita, ameonesha kuwa umetokea baada ya jaribio mbili za Zuckerberg kuuza Twitter, ikiwemo kuingia moja kwa moja na mwenyekiti wake wa msingi, Jack Dorsey. Twitter ilianzisha kazi kwenye New York Stock Exchange jumamosi, kuanzia kwa upesi mkubwa wa 72.69% kwa siku ya kwanza, ikapungua $43. Lakini, sahami zilipungua 7.26% kwa siku ya baadaye hadi $41.64 kwa sababu mapendeleo ya wateja walipungua kidogo. Kwa kinyume na IPO ya Facebook ya 2012 ambayo ilizunguka kwa bei ya $38 na kushuka chini ya hiyo, kwa muda mrefu, Twitter ilichagua kuingiza bei ya $26. Mchanganyiko huu uliwezesha kupongeza kwa muda mrefu, kuzuia uonekano wa kuzingatia bei ya juu. Watawala walipendekeza bei ya $28, lakini Twitter ilichagua kuchukua nafasi ya kusonga. Kwa njia hii, shirika lilipata $1.8 billion, na kuleta zaidi ya $1 billion kwa kutosha — mchanganyiko wa strategia uliokubaliwa kwa ajili ya ustawi. CFO wa Twitter, Anthony Noto, alisema kuwa aliishi kwa makosa ya Facebook, kuzingatia amani ya muda mrefu kuliko kuchukua pesa zaidi kwa muda mfupi.

article_content: Far too often, children with developmental disorders are diagnosed solely based on observable behavior, slotted into broad diagnostic categories, and given generalized treatments that may not address their specific needs. For example, children are sometimes labeled with broad diagnoses like 'autism' or 'attention deficit disorder' after a single psychological evaluation and then prescribed expensive therapies or strong medications with serious long-term side effects. This incomplete diagnosis—or overmedication—can leave underlying conditions untreated, allowing them to worsen and deepening the frustration of both parents and children. Such an approach is akin to diagnosing and treating a heart condition without ever performing a chest X-ray or ECG to examine the heart. The core message of my TED talk was simple: to accurately diagnose any brain-related developmental disorder, we must look directly at the brain. Behavior alone can provide an incomplete or misleading picture. Moreover, when examining the brain, it’s essential to move beyond structure to function. In many cognitive disorders, brain structure remains intact, but its function is impaired. Traditionally, abnormalities in brain function have been detected using electroencephalography (EEG), which measures the brain’s ongoing electrical activity. Standard EEG produces patterns of spikes and waves that clinicians visually inspect for anomalies. However, recent technological advances have led to the development of a pioneering EEG system called Brain Electrical Activity Mapping (BEAM), created at Harvard University by neurologist Dr. Frank Duffy. BEAM enhances traditional EEG by adding sophisticated visual displays and statistical analyses to reveal deeper insights into brain dysfunction. For instance, BEAM can map a patient’s EEG data onto 3D schematic representations of the head and determine whether the brain activity falls outside age-appropriate norms using Statistical Probability Mapping. This technique compares the patient’s EEG to a proprietary database of over 2,000 fully screened, healthy children, making BEAM a uniquely powerful diagnostic tool for neurological conditions. Using BEAM, researchers have found that many children diagnosed with autism are actually experiencing virtually undetectable brain seizures that mimic autistic behaviors. Growing evidence suggests that between one-third and one-half of children with autism exhibit abnormal seizure-like brain activity, and up to one-third may develop epilepsy by adolescence. In some cases, this activity is a consequence of the underlying neurological condition; in others, it coexists with autism. But in certain cases—such as the one I presented at TED—the seizures themselves are the root cause of the symptoms. When treated, these children show remarkable improvements in both speed and degree of recovery. Because symptoms like staring into space or unresponsiveness can be mistaken for autism during behavioral evaluations, such seizure activity would remain undetected without EEG testing. Importantly, not all children with autism or other developmental disorders have seizures or abnormal EEG findings—and for some who do, seizures may not explain all their symptoms. Therefore, I do not advocate replacing behavioral assessments with neurophysiological tests. Rather, I urge their integration to triangulate the true cause of symptoms and enable more precise, effective interventions. Since my TED talk, I’ve been working to make Harvard’s BEAM system more widely accessible—from the United States to India. The surge of inquiries since the talk has accelerated our efforts. My goal is to ensure that affordable, high-quality EEG-based brain function assessments are available to every family worldwide. Until then, parents should know that even a standard digital EEG performed by a local physician could reveal whether seizure activity is contributing to their child’s challenges. My TED talk was less about promoting a specific technology and more about advocating for a fundamental shift in diagnostic approach: to diagnose developmental disorders accurately, we must look directly at the brain. As I say when testing children: 'When we put this magic cap on you, your brain can finally talk to us—and we can finally listen!'
translated_content: Kwa kiasi kikubwa, watoto wenye ugonjwa wa maendeleo huchaguliwa kwa msingi wa tabia zao zilizotazamwa tu, wamepewa alama za kawaida kama 'autism' au 'disorder ya kusikia' na kuchukuliwa mbinu za kawaida zisizoweza kuhakikisha mahitaji yao ya kipekee. Kwa mfano, watoto wengi wanapewa alama za kawaida kama 'autism' au 'attention deficit disorder' baada ya tathmini moja ya psikolojia na kumpa mapema mapinduzi au dawa nyingi zenye mifumo ya muda mrefu yenye hatari. Mchakato huu wa kuchagua kwa kasi au kutoa dawa zaidi ya lazima unaweza kuleta matatizo ya kina bila kuzalisha, kuharibu na kuzidisha ubaya wa wazazi na mtoto. Mchakato huu ni sawa na kuchagua na kuleta upasuwa wa moyo bila kufanya X-ray ya chini au ECG kueleza moyo. Ujumbe wa msingi wa munguanguko yangu kwa TED lilikuwa rahisi: kuchagua kwa akili kwa kila ugonjwa wa maendeleo wa ubongo, ni muhimu kuchunguza ubongo. Tabia pekee inaweza kutoa picha ya kutosha au ya kusisimua. Pia, wakati unachunguza ubongo, ni muhimu kushuka juu ya mradi wake kwa kazi yake. Hii ni kwa sababu mara nyingi katika ugonjwa wa kishiria, mradi wa ubongo unaishi bila changamoto, lakini kazi yake iko na changamoto. Kwa kawaida, vimelea vya kazi ya ubongo vinapatikana kwa kutumia EEG (electroencephalography), ambayo inafanya maelezo ya mzunguko wa umeme uliotengenezwa na ubongo. EEG ya awali inatoa mstari wa miguu na miguu ambayo huzingatiwa kwa macho ya kupata vimelea. Lakini, baada ya mabadiliko mengine ya teknolojia, mbinu ya EEG ya kwanza ya Brain Electrical Activity Mapping (BEAM) ilianzishwa na Dr. Frank Duffy katika Harvard University. Mbinu hii inaongeza mifumo ya kielekezo na uchambuzi wa kihisabati kwa rekodi za EEG ya awali ili kutoa habari zaidi kuhusu kosa la ubongo. Kwa mfano, BEAM haibaini tu rekodi za EEG za mtoto kwenye sarafu ya 3D ya kichwani, bali inaweza kuhesabu ikiwa EEG imechukua nje ya kina ya umri wa mtoto. Hii inafanywa kwa mbinu inayoitwa Statistical Probability Mapping, ambayo inaingiza rekodi za EEG za mtoto kwenye databasi ya EEG za watoto wote wanaotazamwa kwa kina. Kwa kutumia BEAM, wetu wamepata kwamba watoto wengi waliochaguliwa kama 'autism' hawana kwa kweli kosa la ubongo la kugusa ambalo linaweza kutoa tabia za autism. Kwa ujumla, kuna adhabu kubwa ya kwamba kati ya kumi na tatu na nusu ya watoto wenye autism wanaweza kuwa na kipindi cha kugusa cha ubongo, na kati ya kumi na tatu ya watoto wenye autism wanaweza kuchukua epilepsy kwa muda wa utoto wa kijana. Katika baadhi ya hali, kipindi hiki cha kugusa kinaweza kuwa matokeo tu ya kosa la kina la ubongo ambalo linatoa autism; katika wingi, kina pamoja na autism. Lakini katika baadhi ya hali, kama nilivyosema kwa TED, kugusa ni kwa kweli sababu ya tabia za mtoto, na wakati inatunza, kuzalisha na mchakato wa kuzalisha kwa watoto hawa ni mpya sana. Kwa sababu tabia kama kudanganya kwenye nafasi au kushindwa kujibu zinaweza kuchanganyikiwa kama autism katika tathmini za tabia, hatutakuwa tajua kipindi cha kugusa cha ubongo bila testi ya EEG. Hata hivyo, watoto wengi waliochaguliwa kama autism na ugonjwa wa maendeleo wengine hawana kugusa yoyote au mazingira ya EEG. Na kwa baadhi ya wale ambao wana, hii haikusababisha majibu yote ya tabia yao. Kwa hiyo, si ninaomba kurekebisha tathmini za tabia na mbinu za fiziolojia ya ubongo, bali ninaomba kuchanganya zao ili kuchunguza kwa kina sababu ya tabia za mtoto, na kuhakikisha mbinu zaidi za kina na ya kuvutia. Baada ya munguanguko yangu kwa TED, nimekaa kufanya BEAM ya Harvard ikawa zaidi elezani—kutoka Marekani hadi India. Kwa sababu ya mchanganyiko wa maswali ya sasa, tunakaa kwa kasi zaidi. Nia yangu ni kuwa na mifumo mengi duniani kote ambayo ni rahisi na inawezekana kwa kila familia. Mpaka sasa, ni muhimu kwa wazazi kujua kwamba testi ya EEG ya kawaida inayofanywa na daktari wa mahali pamoja inaweza kuchunguza ikiwa kugusa ya ubongo inaingiza katika tabia za mtoto yao. Hata hivyo, munguanguko yangu kwa TED haikuwa na lengo la kuhakikisha mbinu yoyote au teknolojia, bali kudai muhimu wa njia fulani ya kuchagua ugonjwa huo. Njia hii ni rahisi: ili kuchagua kwa kina ugonjwa wa maendeleo, tunapaswa kuchunguza ubongo kwa kina. Au, kwa kusema neno nililotumia wakati ninatathmini watoto: 'Wakati tunavuta kipande hiki cha kihaya kwenye mwili wako, ubongo wako aweze kusema kwa wetu, na wetu tuweze kusikia!'

article_content: During a cross-country meet in North Carolina, high school junior Connor Callihan refused to quit — even after shattering his tibia in three places just five feet from the finish line. Competing for T.C. Roberson High School in the Mountain Athletic Conference, he collapsed moments before crossing the line but crawled the remaining distance, enduring what he described as the worst pain he’d ever felt. 'This was my last race of the year,' Callihan later said from his hospital bed. 'I just had to finish for my team.' His determination didn’t go unnoticed. Olympic sprinter Manteo Mitchell, who famously finished his 4x400m relay leg in the 2012 London Games despite breaking his own tibia, reached out to call him a 'good kid' and offered words of encouragement. Surgeons at Mission Hospitals in Asheville performed surgery on Tuesday, inserting three metal rods to stabilize the fracture. Callihan’s mother, Stephanie, said he had been complaining of leg discomfort for days leading up to the race but insisted on competing anyway. His story has since become a symbol of grit in high school athletics.

Alichukua mshale wa T.C. Roberson High School katika Michuano ya Mountain Athletic, aliporuka dakika moja kabla ya kushuka, lakini akakimbia kwa mkono kwa umbali huo uliobaki, akisubiri dhambi ambayo alivyoeleza kuwa ilikuwa dhambi bora zaidi aliyojivuna. 'Hii ilikuwa michezo yangu ya mwisho wa mwaka,' alisema Callihan kutoka kwenye chumba cha kituo. 'Ninafanya kazi yangu kwa timu yangu.' Ujasiri wake hakuwa na kila mtu. Mwanamitindo wa Olimpiki Manteo Mitchell, ambaye alikamilisha sura yake ya 4x400m katika Michuano ya Olimpiki ya London 2012 bila kuharibu tibia yake, alinunua mawazo ya kushukuru kwa kusema yeye ni 'mtu mzuri' na kutoa msaada wake. Wizara wa kirumia wa Mission Hospitals nchini Asheville walifanya kuchukua kwa Jumatatu, kuingiza rodu tatu za metali ili kusimama tibia. article_content: Entertainment Weekly has confirmed that Michael McKean is joining the cast of 'Better Call Saul', AMC’s highly anticipated prequel to 'Breaking Bad'. McKean, known for his iconic roles in 'This Is Spinal Tap' and 'Laverne & Shirley', will portray Dr. Thurber — a brilliant but eccentric lawyer whose personal quirks complicate his professional life. The series dives into the early days of Saul Goodman (played by Bob Odenkirk), the morally flexible attorney who later becomes entangled with drug kingpin Walter White (Bryan Cranston). Joining him is Jonathan Banks reprising his role as the stoic private investigator Mike Ehrmantraut, a fan-favorite from the original series. Scheduled to debut this November, the show builds on the gritty realism of 'Breaking Bad' while expanding its world with fresh, complex characters. McKean, who recently appeared in HBO’s 'Family Tree' and guest-starred on 'Happy Endings' and 'Law & Order: SVU', brings a unique blend of comedic timing and dramatic depth to the role.

article_content: Five young friends lost their lives in a devastating car crash in Burbank, California, early Saturday morning. Their vehicle veered off a road and erupted in flames, trapping them inside. The victims—identified through community tributes as Sameer Nevarez, Sugey Cuevas, Stephen Stoll, Malak Hariri, and Sebastian Forero—were all 22 years old or younger. The sole survivor, 18-year-old Savannah Underwood, was found approximately 50 yards from the charred Nissan sedan by police shortly after 4 a.m. on September 28, 2013. She sustained a broken leg and non-life-threatening injuries and was receiving treatment at Los Angeles County Medical Center. Her father was by her side, according to Sergeant Darin Ryburn. All five victims were close friends who attended Burbank High School and graduated in recent years. The community, including classmates and families, expressed profound grief through heartfelt online messages and memorials. One tribute read: 'Heaven gained five angels today—they gave us clear skies and a beautiful day. Rest in peace. You will never be forgotten.' Malak Hariri’s family described her as intelligent, kind, and respectful. 'She never had problems at home,' said relative Suhilah Hariri. The accident occurred on a curving stretch of road with a posted speed limit of 45 mph, though drivers frequently exceed 70 mph. Authorities confirmed previous incidents on this stretch and are investigating whether speeding contributed to the crash. Fire Battalion Chief Ron Barone stated that by the time emergency crews arrived, there was 'absolutely no possibility of any rescue whatsoever.'

Wale waliofariki—waliojulikana kwa maombi ya jamii kama Sameer Nevarez, Sugey Cuevas, Stephen Stoll, Malak Hariri, na Sebastian Forero—wote walikuwa na miaka 22 au chini. Mtu tu ambaye amekaa hai ni Savannah Underwood, aliyekuwa na miaka 18, ambaye alipatikana karibu na 50 yadi kutoka kwenye gari lililofungua na polisi baada ya saa 4. Alipata miguu mmoja imevunjika na ugonjwa usio na hatari ya kifo, na alikuwa amefanywa matibabu katika Kituo cha Afya cha Los Angeles County. Kifafa kilikua katika sehemu ya barabara yenye kikomo cha kasi cha 45 mph, lakini mashine yanayosafiria kwa kasi karibu na 70 mph. article_content: A former San Antonio kindergarten teacher, Cynthia Ambrose, has been sentenced to 30 days in jail and two years of probation for instructing her students to physically assault a 6-year-old boy, Aiden Neely, in May 2012. Ambrose, then teaching at Salinas Elementary School, told her class to line up and hit Neely — who had been bullying another student — so they could show him 'how it feels to be bullied.' The assault continued until the seventh student struck him hard enough to make him cry. His teacher, Barbara Ramirez, witnessed the incident and reported it to the school principal two weeks later. Ambrose was convicted in June 2013 of official oppression, a misdemeanor. Prosecutors originally sought a 90-day sentence but accepted 30 days after the judge imposed probation. During sentencing, State District Judge Sid Harle called the act 'a parent’s worst nightmare,' adding, 'They send their children... and entrust you with them.' Ambrose, who broke down in tears, stated she was not a 'nasty person' and hoped all parties would find peace. Her defense argued the event was a 'misunderstanding' and that few students remembered it. Ramirez was granted immunity in exchange for her testimony. Principal Jeffrey Large said he had never seen such behavior in his 30 years in education. Prosecutor Patrick Ballantyne emphasized this was not a bullying case, but a case of child abuse. The judge allowed Ambrose to serve her jail time on weekends or through work release.

Ambrose, ambaye alihudhuria shule ya msingi ya Salinas, alisema kwa darasa lake kuchukua mfululizo na kupiga Neely — ambaye alikuwa amevaa mwanafunzi mwingine — ili kumwona jinsi 'kushikamana' kwa mwanafunzi mwingine. Ambrose alikadhibishwa Juni 2013 kwa uongozi wa udhalimu, ni masharti ya chini. Ramirez alipewa haki ya kushindwa kwa ajili ya testimo yake. Mkuu wa shule Jeffrey Large alisema hakuona jambo kama hili katika miaka 30 yake ya kazi. Wakili wa serikali Patrick Ballantyne alisema hii si jambo la kushikamana, bali jambo la kuvaa watoto. Hakimu aliruhusu Ambrose kufanya muda wake wa umbo la kijiji kwa muda wa mwezi au kuchukua nafasi ya kazi.
